items.body: China And St. Augustine - Gavekal Research China And St. Augustine Louis-Vincent Gave Gavekal Research | 23 Oct 2026 Back in the summer of 2015, the Chinese government decided that equity markets had risen too far, too fast. The rug was pulled from under margin lending and various restrictions were put in place that brought the unfolding raging equity bull market to an abrupt end. By January 2024, the Chinese government reversed course and decided that Chinese equity prices had fallen far enough. Beijing intervened in the market (see Chinese Policies And Chinese Equities ) and put a floor under domestic markets. Equities duly rallied, delivering very solid returns for 2024 and 2025. However, over the past year, Chinese equity market returns have been fairly dismal. In fact, Chinese equity markets have now fallen for 10 consecutive weeks, a feat they had never achieved before. items.body: Council on Foreign Relations Articles By experts and staff Updated October 11, 2026 12:00 a.m. Brad W. Setser CFR Expert Whitney Shepardson Senior Fellow There is an argument—made in the recent Geneva Report and by various former IMF officials —that China’s current export surge is the simple consequence of the housing downturn and the resulting weakness in Chinese internal demand.* The weakness in the RMB in this story is entirely incidental to the increase in exports, which is, more or less, a mechanical response to weak internal demand. items.author: Brad Setser
items.title_en: De-reservification, Not De-dollarization | Council on Foreign Relations
items.summary_en: The world isn’t moving away from the dollar. It is shifting its dollars from traditional reserves to state banks, pension funds, and other quasi-sovereign investors.
items.body: Council on Foreign Relations By experts and staff Published September 15, 2026 8:37 a.m. Brad W. Setser CFR Expert Whitney Shepardson Senior Fellow This is a joint blog with Alex Etra , Senior Macro Strategist and head of Flow of Funds at Vanda Research . The IMF’s data on the currency composition of foreign exchange (FX) reserves is scrutinized carefully for any signs that the world is shifting way from the dollar. Yet it doesn’t really matter that much if the dollar’s share of reserves has shifted from 56.5 percent to 57 percent. The ink-to-impact ratio of the quarterly reporting on the latest COFER data is all off. Neither the stock of global reserves nor the stock of dollar reserves has changed much in the last ten years. The action is elsewhere. China’s state banks (per the Bank of International Settlements) have almost as many foreign assets as the central bank (PBOC). Japan’s Government Pension Investment Fund (GPIF) has almost as many foreign assets ( $986 billion ) as the government has FX reserves ($1.1 trillion at the end of August). items.author: Rhodium Group
items.title_en: As Europe Dithers, the Cost of Derisking from China Rises
items.summary_en: The cost of confronting China will be high. But the cost of waiting—for Europe’s economy, security, and sovereignty—could be far higher.
items.body: In March 2023, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called on Europe to unite behind a policy of economic derisking from China. In a speech in Brussels, she warned about Europe’s deepening dependencies on Chinese rare earths, called for more robust trade measures to protect European industry from unfair competition and for new tools to restrict the flow of sensitive technologies to China. More than two and a half years later, it is clear that her warning has gone largely unheeded. Today, Europe is more dependent on critical inputs from China than ever before. China’s export restrictions on critical minerals and chips produced by the Chinese-owned Dutch firm Nexperia have hit European companies in the auto, medical, and defense sectors in recent months, laying bare Europe’s failure to derisk. EU trade defense instruments cover less than 10% of imports from China despite evidence of systemic state support for Chinese companies and an economic model that has relied for years on flooding global markets with cheap goods . Efforts to restrict the flow of artificial intelligence, quantum, and chip technologies to China have stalled amid resistance from European member states

items.summary_en: Rhodium Group is a founding member, with Rhodium Partner Kate Larsen appointed as Director of Data and Analysis of the NEIS Center.
items.body: This week marked the launch of the New Energy Industrial Strategy Center, a new hub dedicated to harnessing advanced energy technologies to strengthen key industries vital to broader economic and national interests. The New Energy Industrial Strategy (NEIS) Center is building a global network of researchers, policymakers, and private sector stakeholders who are advancing industrial strategies that leverage advanced energy systems to support the industries needed for growing, security-conscious nations. The NEIS Center is hosted by RMI and supported by The William and Flora Hewlett Foundation. Rhodium Group is a founding member, with Rhodium Partner Kate Larsen appointed as Director of Data and Analysis of the NEIS Center. Data and analytics from Rhodium’s Global Clean Investment Monitor and China Cross-Border Monitor will be critical inputs for decision-makers navigating this new era of clean energy competition. news_items.summary_en: Beijing seeks to safeguard billions in regional infrastructure and economic investments while hewing to its pledge of non-interference.
news_items.body: Beijing has a formula for tackling African conflicts and hot-button issues, and during a meeting this month with Togolese leader Faure Gnassingbe, Chinese President Xi Jinping outlined it in four principles linking peace to development. The principles entail focusing on African-led security free from outside intervention; upholding sovereignty and UN Charter principles; rejecting force and sanctions and favouring ceasefires through dialogue; and focusing on both immediate security concerns and long-term development. Asked on Monday whether the principles could be applied to northern Ethiopia and heightened tensions with neighbouring Eritrea, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said they offered “practical guidance” for the Horn of Africa. Days later, a joint statement following a meeting between Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and his Djiboutian counterpart, Abdoulkader Houssein Omar, said China would continue to play a constructive role in mediating regional disputes through its existing Horn of Africa peace-and-development initiative, subject to the wishes of the countries concerned. news_items.summary_en: Smart coolers offer seamless grab-and-go convenience but local operators say city’s distinct economic factors may stall widespread adoption.
news_items.body: Sherry Shum has embraced a new shopping routine after finding a smart vending machine near her home in Chai Wan. The 37-year-old retail worker uses her phone to scan a QR code, opens the smart machine’s door, picks up a bottle of Coca-Cola, an oolong tea and a pack of potato chips, closes it and walks away with HK$60 (US$7.70) worth of goods. The whole process is so seamless that the only time she spends is deciding what to buy. The moment Shum takes an item from the shelf, the machine detects the product based on its appearance and debits her account. Once she shuts the door, the bill is settled via the payment method she selected before opening it. “I buy things basically every day … I can grab multiple items at once after just opening the door,” she said. “The open-door machines are more convenient because you do not have to wait for items to drop one by one from traditional machines that sometimes get stuck.” For decades, vending machines have evolved from simple dispensers of bottled or canned drinks into smart retail points that combine digital payments and data-driven consumer insights. news_items.summary_en: Even as the region’s economic downturn is expected to worsen, Gulf states are slated to spend tens of billions of dollars on infrastructure.
news_items.body: Before the outbreak of the war triggered by the US-Israeli attack on Iran in February, the Gulf monarchies were living the prosperity dream that was the envy of the world. Their hydrocarbon-fuelled economies were glitzy oases of growth, inoculated from the conflict in Gaza that had rocked other parts of the Middle East for several years. Underpinned by decades-old US security guarantees and conflict mediation by billionaire sheikhs, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar cultivated images as peaceful lands of opportunity as they invested staggering amounts of money in economic diversification programmes. Backed by sovereign wealth funds with trillions of dollars invested mostly in the West, these leading states of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) embarked on transformative programmes to reposition their economies amid the global transition away from oil and gas. Similar diversification initiatives were also happening in Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain, the other three GCC members. news_items.summary_en: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said the government would explore nuclear power and boost global partnerships for energy security.
news_items.body: Singapore expects all parties who have signed commercial contracts for gas supplies to “honour their commitments”, said Prime Minister Lawrence Wong on Sunday after Indonesia cut its exports. Speaking at the People’s Action Party (PAP) convention, Wong added that Singapore’s gas importer will take the necessary steps to protect its rights and interests. Indonesia began reducing natural gas exports to Singapore on Saturday. Indonesia’s upstream oil and gas regulator SKK Migas said the move was to divert more supplies to domestic electricity needs. Singapore’s Energy Market Authority said the reduction of 31 million standard cubic feet of gas a day amounts to less than 2 per cent of Singapore’s total daily gas demand. About 95 per cent of Singapore’s electricity is generated using natural gas and it imports a significant amount of this gas through pipelines from Indonesia. “The gas supplies are covered by commercial contracts. We expect all parties to honour their commitments and Singapore’s gas importer will take the necessary steps to protect its rights and interests under these contracts,” Wong said. news_items.body: A woman in eastern China has been devotedly caring for her daughter-in-law for 17 years, ever since she fell into a vegetative state, moving social media users. The younger woman, surnamed Xu, fell into a vegetative state in 2009 after being struck by a truck in her village in Qingyun county, Shandong province. The accident happened just one month after she got married, Shandian News reported. Since then, her mother-in-law, Xuan Fengying, has cared for her around the clock. “She married my son, so she’s my child. How could I abandon her?” the 68-year-old Xuan was quoted as saying. Xuan fed Xu liquid food one spoonful at a time, and each meal took an hour. She also helped Xu turn over more than 10 times a day to prevent bedsores. Other caregiving tasks included washing Xu after she became incontinent and regularly massaging her muscles. Xuan also talked to Xu about news from the family and their village, played her favourite songs, and repeatedly called her name. Several years ago, Xu miraculously emerged from the vegetative state. news_items.title_en: Fandom vs flag: why young Chinese embrace Japanese pop culture but reject war-era symbols | South China Morning Post
news_items.summary_en: For many on the mainland, the recent rising sun flag incident and controversies like it show a fondness for anime and manga only goes so far.
news_items.body: Young Chinese people enjoy Japanese pop culture such as anime and music, but many draw a firm line at symbols of Japanese militarism. That line was tested recently at Moscow State University, where Chinese students confronted a classmate wearing Japan’s rising sun flag in class and called for his repatriation, state-run newspaper Global Times reported on Sunday. Many countries, including China, view the flag as a symbol of Japanese militarism and aggression. Japan’s Self-Defence Forces still use the flag today. The October 14 incident sparked an online backlash against the Chinese student and praise for those who reported him, following commentaries by People’s Daily, the Communist Party’s official newspaper, and the People’s Liberation Army. “A disgrace to the Chinese people,” read one of the top comments under a post by Jun Zhengping, a social media account run by the PLA. Among those condemning the student were people who enjoyed Japanese pop culture, including Lucy Huang, 24. news_items.title_en: Why more Japanese women are choosing ‘silver divorce’ after decades of marriage | South China Morning Post
news_items.summary_en: As children leave home and with changing pension rules, more older Japanese women are choosing to walk away from distant marriages.
news_items.body: Ayumi lives alone in a spacious suburban house originally bought to raise a family, her two cats now her only full-time companions. Her two daughters have grown up and left home, and her husband of more than two decades moved out nearly a year ago as they finalise a divorce. For the 62-year-old Kawasaki resident, who spoke on condition that her surname be withheld, this was not how she envisioned her later years. “He worked very long hours, including on weekends, and I was always busy taking care of the house and raising the children,” Ayumi said. “I think we worked well as a team at the beginning, but somewhere along the way, we just stopped talking like we had before.” The marriage had its fair share of ups and downs – financial stress during their daughters’ university years and the deaths of their respective parents. But the final break came when the girls left home. “It felt like we were almost strangers with nothing in common,” she said. “Before, we had always put our children first. news_items.title_en: Opinion | Hong Kong needs a civil service fit for a changed world | South China Morning Post
news_items.summary_en: Beyond administrative expertise, civil servants must now master technology, cross-departmental cooperation and strategic flexibility.
news_items.body: Hong Kong’s civil service has long enjoyed a reputation for efficiency, professionalism and probity. It has also been a pillar of stability, particularly during the transition from British to Chinese rule. Outside the general and administrative grades, many civil servants spend much of their careers in relatively specialised areas of responsibility. This allows them to develop deep expertise and makes them dependable regulators and administrators. However, it can also make it harder to adapt when new challenges cut across established departmental boundaries. Recent events have put this model under scrutiny. The fire that engulfed Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po last November, claiming 168 lives and destroying more than a thousand homes, raised grave questions about building safety and regulatory oversight. Subsequent construction scandals involving luxury homes and public housing estates, together with concerns over lift installations at a major public hospital and in numerous other buildings, have further tested public confidence in the government. news_items.title_en: School bullying cases in Hong Kong rise 32% to nearly 500 a year | South China Morning Post
news_items.summary_en: Youth group attributes increase to heightened mental health awareness, but also students struggling to distinguish jokes from bullying.
news_items.body: Hong Kong schools handled an average of 496 bullying cases each academic year from 2022 to 2025 – a 32 per cent jump compared with the previous three years, according to the Education Bureau. A youth group attributed the increase to greater reporting driven by heightened mental health awareness, but also students struggling to distinguish playful jokes from bullying. According to the bureau, public primary and secondary schools recorded an average of 496 bullying cases each year between 2022 and 2025, up 32 per cent from the 377 recorded annually from 2019 to 2022. The bureau told the Legislative Council in 2023 that the number of cases involving school bullying, including cyberbullying, from the 2019-20 to 2021-22 school years was 411, 306 and 413 respectively. The average number for these three school years was 377. The figures were based on information contained in the bureau’s annual questionnaire surveys on guidance and discipline cases in schools. The bureau did not provide any annual breakdown for the years between 2022 and 2025. news_items.title_en: Singapore embraces AI for cyber defence, with one caveat: breach transparency | South China Morning Post
news_items.summary_en: The city state will take a ‘pragmatic’ approach to AI adoption as it seeks to bolster protection for its critical infrastructure.
news_items.body: Singapore is turning to major technology firms to strengthen its cyber defences, even as it presses them for greater transparency over security breaches – a balancing act facing regional governments as they seek to harness artificial intelligence while guarding against the risks it introduces. Those risks were highlighted by an AI agent linked to OpenAI that gained unauthorised access to files on an Australian government website earlier this year, raising questions over how quickly companies disclose security incidents as AI systems become more capable and autonomous. At a summit earlier this month, Singapore launched a refreshed cybersecurity strategy that would see it progressively deploy AI across its cyber defence operations and work with industry partners to accelerate adoption, as it seeks to bolster protection for its critical infrastructure. The city state would take a “pragmatic” approach to AI adoption, allowing it to choose between the “best available” models, K. Shanmugam, coordinating minister for national security, said during a speech at Singapore International Cyber Week on October 13. “We will not need to develop our own AI models for every use case. news_items.summary_en: The former US president slammed his successor’s ‘corruption and incompetence’ and blamed his ‘bad decisions’ for the rising cost of living.

news_items.title_en: In Focus | China’s next generation of leaders waiting in the wings for more senior roles | South China Morning Post
news_items.summary_en: A meeting in Beijing this week will lay the groundwork for members of the Communist Party’s seventh generation – or 7G – to take on key roles.
news_items.body: Plenary sessions of the Central Committee, the upper echelon of China’s ruling Communist Party, are major events on the country’s political calendar. In the fourth part of this series, William Zheng looks at how the next generation of the party is being formed. When China’s political elites gather behind closed doors in Beijing for the Communist Party’s fifth plenum on Monday, much of the attention will be on the quiet preparations for allocating hundreds of pivotal roles in next year’s 21st party congress. At the heart of this transition is the rise of the party’s seventh generation – often referred to as the 7G – who were born in the late 1960s and the 1970s and whose ascent will be critical in shaping China’s political trajectory. Xie Maosong, a senior researcher at Tsinghua University’s National Institute of Strategic Studies, said the party was looking for cadres who had “absolute political loyalty, integrity, fighting spirit, technological or ‘hard science’ expertise, grass-roots experience and hardship resilience”. “Just like their predecessors, they must demonstrate unquestioned loyalty and integrity. news_items.title_en: Trump, a critic of early voting, votes early in Florida | South China Morning Post
news_items.summary_en: The US president has reversed course on the practice, hoping to mobilise his base to help Republicans keep control of Congress.
news_items.body: US President Donald Trump cast his ballot for the midterm elections in Palm Beach on Saturday, opting to vote early in his adopted home state of Florida. At rallies ahead of Election Day on November 3, Trump has been urging Republicans to cast their ballots early, reversing course on a practice he has long decried in a bid to mobilise the party’s base in an election that threatens to end their control of Congress. Asked by reporters if he voted for the party line, he said: “Very much so.” The president has regularly questioned the security of early voting methods, claiming without evidence that mail-in ballots, drop boxes and other practices during the 2020 presidential election – which he lost – were used to rig the vote. He has also called for one-day, in-person voting on Election Day. “The US attorney found potentially hundreds of thousands of illicit votes,” Trump told reporters. Earlier this month, the US Justice Department sued California for allegedly failing to join an effort to verify the status of 20,000 suspected non-citizens to prevent any fraudulent ballots from being counted. news_items.summary_en: US firms offer cash and shares on their own terms while Asian economies still rely on creating jobs to share the dividends of growth.
news_items.body: On October 18, Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) laboratory preparing one of the largest listings in history, committed 5 per cent of its shares to a public benefit fund. The next day, Elon Musk promised one SpaceX share, next year, for “every kid in America” – about US$10.6 billion for some 73 million children. The offers differ in who holds the shares. Anthropic’s will sit in an entity the company owns, spent on the public’s behalf; Musk’s would land, by a route he has not explained, in a child’s name. Should the public own the companies AI makes rich? Silicon Valley has begun answering yes, on its own terms. This came a week after International Monetary Fund managing director Kristalina Georgieva described AI as a “slow-moving tsunami”, shifting income from labour to capital, that could augment, downgrade or eliminate 40 per cent of jobs worldwide. She spoke in Bangkok; Asia is where economic growth has long depended on creating jobs. America shares growth through wages too, but 62 per cent of adults also own shares. news_items.summary_en: The SpaceX CEO says Kyiv’s forces had used the civilian commercial service for deadly offensive drone strikes.
news_items.body: Elon Musk said on Saturday that his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine, disrupting operations that the country relies on to defend itself against Russia. Musk’s admission on social media came after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said that Ukraine’s access to Starlink and Starshield satellite links has been restored to the speeds it had before restrictions that disrupted frontline operations for more than a week. Questions have persisted since last week about who ordered the interruptions to the Musk-made satellite internet system that Kyiv has relied on for years to counter Moscow’s attacks. “The speeds are now where they need to be,” Zelensky said on social media, adding that restoration began overnight and was sufficient by Saturday morning, improving frontline logistics and defence against Russian jet-powered Shahed drones. news_items.title_en: German man detained after fire wrecks Hitler’s ‘Eagle’s Nest’ mountain retreat | South China Morning Post
news_items.summary_en: Firefighters battled to put out flames at the former guest house for top Nazi officials, high up in the Bavarian Alps.
news_items.body: Firefighters battled on Saturday to put out flames that tore through Adolf Hitler’s “Eagle’s Nest” mountain retreat while police detained a suspect who investigators said may have psychiatric problems. The alarm was raised late on Friday at the former guest house for top Nazi officials, 1,834 metres (6,000 feet) high in the Bavarian Alps. As snow fell on the Alpine peak, the Eagle’s Nest was still engulfed in flames at dawn on Saturday, and fire chief Michael Brandl told a press conference the last elements of the inferno were being put out during the afternoon. No one has entered the building because of fears it could collapse, Brandl added. “We are very lucky that there are no injuries,” Brandl said. Some 200 firefighters were mobilised for the operation at the Kehlsteinhaus residence on a summit above Obersalzberg in southern Germany that draws some 350,000 visitors a year, according to Bavarian state authorities. Authorities said access had been difficult after the fire alarm went off at 9.50pm. Heavy rain was followed by a snowstorm and then violent winds hit the mountains. news_items.summary_en: Suspect, 34, arrested on suspicion of cruelty to animals and possession of an offensive weapon.
news_items.body: Police have arrested a 34-year-old man who allegedly mixed rat poison into food left for stray cats in a Kowloon park and was found in possession of a knife. The force said it received a report at around 3.30am on Saturday that a man was suspected of putting poison in cat food that animal welfare volunteers had placed near tennis courts in Shek Kip Mei Park. Officers arrived at the scene and seized a packet of suspected rat poison and a fruit knife measuring around 14cm (5.5 inches) in length from the man. “Following a preliminary investigation, the man was arrested on suspicion of cruelty to animals and possession of an offensive weapon and is currently being detained for further investigation,” police said. The Sham Shui Po district crime squad is handling the investigation. Animal welfare volunteers said they first discovered someone appearing to poison food and water left for stray cats last month. A social media user said he installed a surveillance camera on a tree in the park and realised the suspect poisoned food and water at around 3am every Saturday. news_items.title_en: Saudi strikes kill 11 in Yemen as Houthi missiles target Saudi cities | South China Morning Post
news_items.summary_en: Houthi media reported a series of ‘Saudi enemy air strikes’ targeting Sanaa, shortly after the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two missiles.
news_items.body: Houthi media reported that Saudi strikes killed 11 people in Yemeni capital Sanaa on Saturday, shortly after the Saudi-led coalition fighting them said it had intercepted two missiles targeting Saudi cities. The Houthis’ Al-Masirah outlet reported a series of “Saudi enemy air strikes” targeting Sanaa, including one on a house that killed at least four people and wounded several others. A separate strike at a residence building for cement factory workers in the Sanaa governorate killed six women and one child and wounded three others, the broadcaster said. Yemen’s civil war, pitting the Iran-backed Houthis against the Saudi-supported and internationally recognised government, had been dormant since a ceasefire in 2022, but erupted again in July as the wider Middle East war roiled the region. The strikes in Yemen came after the Saudi-led coalition announced it had intercepted two missiles fired by the Houthis towards Taif and Yanbu, in the kingdom’s west. Earlier, Riyadh’s civil defence agency broadcast warnings of “potential danger” for four western regions, including Taif and Yanbu as well Mecca, home to Islam’s holiest city, and Yanbu. The alerts were all rescinded minutes later.

news_items.summary_en: Two large metal stands removed following visit by tourism commissioner, lawmaker and councillor to site.
news_items.body: Parts of two installations in a controversial lighting project along a walking trail on The Peak have been removed, days after Hong Kong’s tourism authorities pledged to balance the community’s needs and said the scheme was not “set in stone”. The removals came hours after Commissioner for Tourism Ann Chan Wai-yan inspected the site on Saturday morning with a lawmaker and a district councillor, following an outcry from residents who accused the Hong Kong Tourism Board of removing trees and flowers to make way for the installations. When the South China Morning Post visited The Peak late on Saturday afternoon, two large metal stands that had held industrial-grade projectors had been removed, leaving only their grey foundational blocks and some bolts, which were not cordoned off. A security guard near the park on the Harlech Road and Lugard Road circular walk confirmed that the two structures had been removed that afternoon. But a smaller metal stand with a projector remained cordoned off near a pavilion. The guard said it had been tested but was not yet fully operational. news_items.title_en: China’s J-20 stealth jet designers plan to put powerful radar into aircraft wing | South China Morning Post
news_items.summary_en: Military aircraft designers propose a wing-mounted early-warning radar to expand coverage during air combat.
news_items.body: Fighter jets typically house their main radars behind a radome in the nose, while conventional airborne early-warning aircraft often carry large radar arrays in prominent structures above the fuselage. Although aircraft wings offer a large surface area, their relatively thin cross-sections leave limited internal space for radar equipment. Top Chinese military aircraft designers have now proposed a revolutionary method to integrate large antenna arrays into aircraft wings, using flight manoeuvres and coordinated formations of unmanned aircraft to expand radar coverage. The design was outlined in a study published online on October 10 in the peer-reviewed Chinese journal Measurement & Control Technology, which presented wing-mounted radar as a new approach to building multifunctional, high-performance airborne early-warning systems. “Wing-mounted early-warning radar is a new type of mission payload designed to meet the early-warning needs of distributed air combat,” researcher Ren Yunsong and his team wrote, describing the concept as “a new pathway” to developing systems with strong detection capabilities. body {

}
html body .region-inner {
min-width: 0;
max-width: 100%;
width: auto;
}
h2 {
font-size: 22px;
}
a:link {
text-decoration:none;
color: #2288bb;
}
a:visited {
text-decoration:none;
color: #888888;
}
a:hover {
text-decoration:underline;

}
.body-fauxcolumn-outer .fauxcolumn-inner {

_background-image: none;
}
.body-fauxcolumn-outer .cap-top {
position: absolute;
z-index: 1;
height: 400px;
width: 100%;
}
.body-fauxcolumn-outer .cap-top .cap-left {
width: 100%;
background: transparent url(https://resources.blogblog.com/blogblog/data/1kt/simple/gradients_light.png) repeat-x scroll top left;
_background-image: none;
}
.content-outer {

-goog-ms-box-shadow: 0 0 10px #333333;
box-shadow: 0 0 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, .15);

}
.content-inner {
padding: 10px 10px;
}
.content-inner {
background-color: #ffffff;
}
/* Header
----------------------------------------------- */
.header-outer {
background: transparent none repeat-x scroll 0 -400px;
_background-image: none;
}
.Header h1 {
font: normal normal 60px Arial, Tahoma, Helvetica, FreeSans, sans-serif;
color: #3399bb;
text-shadow: -1px -1px 1px rgba(0, 0, 0, .2);
}
.Header h1 a {
color: #3399bb;
}
.Header .description {
font-size: 140%;
color: #777777;
}
.header-inner .Header .titlewrapper {
padding: 22px 30px;
}
.header-inner .Header .descriptionwrapper {
padding: 0 30px;
}
/* Tabs
----------------------------------------------- */
.tabs-inner .section:first-child {
border-top: 1px solid #eeeeee;
}
.tabs-inner .section:first-child ul {
margin-top: -1px;

border-right: 0 solid #eeeeee;
}

margin-top: 0;
margin-left: -30px;
margin-right: -30px;
}

}

border-left: none;
}

text-decoration: none;
}
/* Columns
----------------------------------------------- */
.main-outer {
border-top: 0 solid #eeeeee;
}
.fauxcolumn-left-outer .fauxcolumn-inner {
border-right: 1px solid #eeeeee;
}
.fauxcolumn-right-outer .fauxcolumn-inner {
border-left: 1px solid #eeeeee;
}

----------------------------------------------- */
div.widget > h2,
div.widget h2.title {
margin: 0 0 1em 0;
font: normal bold 11px Arial, Tahoma, Helvetica, FreeSans, sans-serif;
color: #000000;
}
/* Widgets
----------------------------------------------- */
.widget .zippy {
color: #999999;

}

list-style: none;
}
/* Posts
----------------------------------------------- */
h2.date-header {
font: normal bold 11px Arial, Tahoma, Helvetica, FreeSans, sans-serif;
}
.date-header span {
background-color: transparent;
color: #222222;
padding: inherit;
letter-spacing: inherit;
margin: inherit;
}
.main-inner {
padding-top: 30px;
padding-bottom: 30px;
}
.main-inner .column-center-inner {
padding: 0 15px;
}

margin: 0 15px;
}
.post {
margin: 0 0 25px 0;
}

}
.post-body {

position: relative;
}
.post-body img, .post-body .tr-caption-container, .Profile img, .Image img,
.BlogList .item-thumbnail img {

padding: 5px;
}
.post-body .tr-caption-container {
color: #222222;
}
.post-body .tr-caption-container img {
padding: 0;
background: transparent;
border: none;
-moz-box-shadow: 0 0 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, .1);
-webkit-box-shadow: 0 0 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, .1);
box-shadow: 0 0 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, .1);
}
.post-header {
margin: 0 0 1.5em;
line-height: 1.6;
font-size: 90%;
}
.post-footer {
margin: 20px -2px 0;
padding: 5px 10px;
color: #666666;
background-color: #f9f9f9;
border-bottom: 1px solid #eeeeee;
line-height: 1.6;
font-size: 90%;
}

padding-top: 1.5em;
border-top: 1px solid #eeeeee;
background-position: 0 1.5em;
}
#comments .comment-author:first-child {
padding-top: 0;
border-top: none;
}
.avatar-image-container {
margin: .2em 0 0;
}
#comments .avatar-image-container img {
border: 1px solid #eeeeee;
}
/* Comments
----------------------------------------------- */
.comments .comments-content .icon.blog-author {
background-repeat: no-repeat;
background-image: url(data:image/png;base64,);
}
.comments .comments-content .loadmore a {
border-top: 1px solid #999999;
border-bottom: 1px solid #999999;
}
.comments .comment-thread.inline-thread {
background-color: #f9f9f9;
}
.comments .continue {
border-top: 2px solid #999999;
}

border-left: 1px solid #eeeeee;
}
.blog-pager {
background: transparent none no-repeat scroll top center;
}

background-color: #ffffff;

}
.footer-outer {
border-top: 0 dashed #bbbbbb;
}

body.mobile  {
background-size: auto;
}

margin-left: 0;
margin-right: 0;
}
.mobile .post {
margin: 0;
}

margin: 0;
}
.mobile .date-header span {
padding: 0.1em 10px;
margin: 0 -10px;
}
.mobile h3.post-title {
margin: 0;
}
.mobile .blog-pager {
background: transparent none no-repeat scroll top center;
}
.mobile .footer-outer {
border-top: none;
}

background-color: #ffffff;
}
.mobile-index-contents {
color: #222222;
}
.mobile-link-button {
background-color: #2288bb;
}
.mobile-link-button a:link, .mobile-link-button a:visited {

}
.mobile .tabs-inner .section:first-child {
border-top: none;
